The Shannonsiders{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/galway-issue-statement-of-intent-as-tribesmen-hand-limerick-first-defeat-since-july-2019-40431815.html|title=Galway issue statement of intent as Tribesmen hand Limerick first defeat since July 2019|work=[[Irish Independent]]|date=16 May 2021|quote=There was also a stirring cameo from Joe Canning, making his first appearance since last year's All-Ireland semi-final defeat to the Shannonsiders.}} | county board = [[Limerick GAA]] | manager = [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]] | captain = [[Cian Lynch]]{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0112/1490370-lynch-replaces-hannon-as-limerick-name-new-captain/|title=Cian Lynch replaces Declan Hannon as Limerick name new captain|publisher=RTÉ|date=12 January 2025}} | most appearances = | top scorer = | home venues = [[Gaelic Grounds]], [[Limerick]] | shc = [[2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Semi-finals|2026]] Winners | last championship title = [[2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2026]] | nhl division = 1A (1st in [[2026 National Hurling League#Division 1A|2026]]) | last league title = [[2026 National Hurling League|2026]] | pattern_la1 = _whiteborder | pattern_b1 = _vneckwhite | pattern_ra1 = _whiteborder | pattern_sh1 = _adidasonwhite | pattern_so1 = _whitestripe | leftarm1 = 009900 | body1 = 009900 | rightarm1 = 009900 | shorts1 = 009900 | socks1 = 009900 | pattern_la2 = _goldborder | pattern_b2 = _vneckgreen | pattern_ra2 = _whiteborder | pattern_sh2 = _adidasongreen | pattern_so2 = _greenstripe | leftarm2 = 000000 | bodygreen = 800000 | rightarm2 = 000000 | shorts2 = 000000 | socks2 = 800000 | current = }} The '''Limerick county hurling team''' represents [[County Limerick|Limerick]] in [[hurling]] and is governed by [[Limerick GAA]], the [[County board (Gaelic games)|county board]] of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]. The team competes in the three major annual inter-county competitions; the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] and the [[National Football League (Ireland)|National Hurling League]]. Limerick's home ground is [[Gaelic Grounds|Páirc na nGael]], [[Limerick]]. The team's manager is [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]]. The team last won the Munster Senior Championship in [[2026 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2026]], the All-Ireland Senior Championship in [[2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2026]] and the National League in [[2026 National Hurling League|2026]]. ==History== Limerick's first outright success in hurling was achieved when the Kilfinane club defeated [[Kilkenny GAA]] club [[Tullaroan GAA|Tullaroan]] in [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|the final]] of the [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] (SHC). At that time, [[County (Gaelic games)|countie]]s were represented by champion clubs. Limerick won the [[1918 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1918 All-Ireland SHC]], then repeated the feat in the [[1921 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1921 All-Ireland SHC]] when the team won the inaugural [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]]. The team that achieved those wins featured many players who contested eight consecutive [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] (SHC) finals (1917–1924 inclusive), a record that has never been equalled.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}} The 1930s were the salad days{{vague|date=November 2022}}{{clarify|date=November 2022}} of Limerick hurling, an era in which the county won five consecutive [[National Hurling League]] (NHL) titles, a record still unequalled.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}} Those titles were won in [[1933–34 National Hurling League|1933–34]], [[1934–35 National Hurling League|1934–35]], [[1935–36 National Hurling League|1935–36]], [[1936–37 National Hurling League|1936–37]] and [[1937–38 National Hurling League|1937–38]]. Limerick also won four consecutive Munster SHC titles, and remains the only team other than [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] to have done so. After winning All-Ireland SHC titles [[1934 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|in 1934]] and [[1936 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|in 1936]], another All-Ireland SHC title followed [[1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|in 1940]]. The team from this era did much to raise the profile of the sport: whereas around 30,000 people attended the [[1930 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1930 All-Ireland SHC Final]], attendances had risen to 50,000 by the 1940 final and players such as the Mackeys ([[John Mackey (hurler)|John]] and [[Mick Mackey|Mick]]), Ryans ([[Timmy Ryan|Timmy]] and [[Mick Ryan (Limerick hurler)|Mick]]), Clohesseys ([[Dave Clohessy|Dave]] and [[Paddy Clohessy|Paddy]]), [[Bob McConkey]] and [[Paddy Scanlan (hurler)|Paddy Scanlon]] were recalled{{by whom|date=November 2022}} for decades afterwards. Victory in 1940 left Limerick with six All-Ireland SHC titles and as the only team from outside the "big three" (Cork, [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] and [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]]) to have won more than one All-Ireland SHC title. [[Dublin county hurling team|Dublin]] had at that stage also six All-Ireland SHC titles but no native of [[County Dublin|that county]] had played on any of its winning teams. Limerick won a sixth NHL title in [[1946–47 National Hurling League|1946–47]] but success soon became a rarity. Limerick won the [[1970–71 National Hurling League|1970–71 NHL]] title and soon followed this by winning the [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1973 All-Ireland SHC]], its seventh title. Four further NHL titles followed that century: [[1983–84 National Hurling League|1983–84]], [[1984–85 National Hurling League|1984–85]], [[1991–92 National Hurling League|1991–92]] and, lastly, [[1997 National Hurling League|1997]]. In the early 2000s, Limerick won three consecutive [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship]] titles (2000–2002). In 2007, Limerick defeated Tipperary in a Munster SHC semi-final known as the Trilogy, as three games were required to separate the teams. The final scoreline of the second replay was 0–22 to 2–13. An attendance of 30,608 spectators witnessed Limerick defeat Tipperary for the first time since 1996. Limerick had not won a match in the Munster SHC since a 2001 comeback against [[Waterford county hurling team|Waterford]], to a Munster SHC final the team subsequently lost to the "monkey on their back" or, as [[Seamus Hickey]] referred to them, "gorilla", Tipperary.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}} However, Limerick subsequently lost the Munster SHC final to Waterford in [[Thurles]] on 8 July. The team regrouped and, in its All-Ireland SHC quarter-final on 29 July, defeated [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]] by a scoreline of 1–23 to 1–16. [[Andrew O'Shaughnessy (hurler)|Andrew O'Shaughnessy]] was named [[Player of the match|man of the match]]. On 12 August, Limerick played Waterford in the All-Ireland SHC semi-final, a rematch of the Munster SHC final that had been played a month previously. The result, though, was not the same. Limerick defeated Waterford by a scoreline of 5–11 to 2–15. The goals came from [[Donie Ryan]] (2), [[Andrew O'Shaughnessy (hurler)|Andrew O'Shaughnessy]] (2 - one from play and one penalty) and [[Brian Begley (dual player)|Brian Begley]] (1). O'Shaughnessy was again named man of the match. This result meant that Limerick had qualified for the [[2007 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2007 All-Ireland SHC Final]], held at [[Croke Park]] on 2 September. Kilkenny defeated Limerick by a scoreline of 2–19 to 1–15. With many{{who|date=November 2022}} predicting that Limerick would soon secure Munster and All-Ireland SHC titles, the team was drawn against Clare in the first round of the 2008 Munster SHC. However, Clare won by a scoreline of 4–12 to 1–16, eliminating Limerick from the Munster SHC. That result also led to Limerick advancing to a game against [[Offaly county hurling team|Offaly]], as part of a newly revised All-Ireland SHC qualifying system. Limerick lost again, this time by a scoreline of 3–19 to 0–18, and the team's season came to an end. Limerick opened against Waterford in the 2009 Munster SHC, with the game ending in a draw. Limerick narrowly lost the [[Replay (sports)|replay]]. That result led to Limerick advancing to the [[2009 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2009 All-Ireland SHC]] qualifier series, where they defeated [[Wexford county hurling team|Wexford]] and [[Laois county hurling team|Laois]] in tight affairs, then Dublin in an All-Ireland SHC quarter-final, to reach an All-Ireland SHC semi-final against Tipperary. Tipperary won that game comfortably, by 22 points, and Limerick's season was over. In the weeks that followed manager [[Justin McCarthy (hurler)|Justin McCarthy]] dropped 12 players (who only found out via the ''[[Irish Examiner]]'') and a further 12 players withdrew from the panel in protest and refused to return as long as McCarthy was in charge. The Limerick County Board held three meetings in which it was decided McCarthy would be retained. Limerick were [[Promotion and relegation|relegate]]d from Division 1 of the [[2010 National Hurling League|2010 NHL]], losing all eight games. Limerick lost to Cork in the first round of the Munster SHC, then lost to Offaly in a [[2010 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2010 All-Ireland SHC]] qualifier. In total Limerick lost its 10 matches by an average of 15 points. McCarthy subsequently resigned as manager. In September 2010, [[Dónal O'Grady]] was appointed as manager. Limerick improved dramatically in the [[2011 National Hurling League|2011 NHL]], winning nearly every game and being [[Promotion and relegation|promote]]d to Division 1 only to later end up in Division 1B.{{how|date=November 2022}} Limerick lost against Waterford in the Munster SHC, with [[John Mullane (hurler)|John Mullane]] eventually scoring a late goal. Limerick then advanced the [[2011 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2011 All-Ireland SHC]] qualifiers, defeating Wexford and also (comprehensively) defeating [[Antrim county hurling team|Antrim]], to reach an All-Ireland SHC quarter-final against NHL title holder Dublin. Dublin won that game by a scoreline of 3–13 to 0–18, ending Limerick's season. O'Grady resigned as manager a few months later over his determination that he intended to stay as coach for only one year. In October 2011, [[John Allen (hurler)|John Allen]] was appointed as manager. Inadequate fitness levels contributed to defeats against Clare in the Division 1B Final and against Tipperary in the Munster SHC in Allen's first year. However, an extensive specifically designed summer fitness course led to a marked improvement, then a creditable losing performance against Kilkenny in the [[2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2012 All-Ireland SHC]] quarter-final offered hope for 2013. As in 2012, Dublin (managed by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]]) defeated Limerick in the [[2013 National Hurling League|2013 NHL]] Division 1B Final.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dublin-return-to-hurling-s-top-table-at-limerick-s-expense-1.1351663|title=Dublin return to hurling's top table at Limerick's expense|newspaper=The Irish Times|first=Damian|last=Cullen|date=6 April 2013|quote=Dublin manager Anthony Daly celebrates at the final whistle after his side's victory over Limerick in the Allianz Hurling League Division 1B Final at Semple Stadium.}} That summer would bring a pitch invasion by spectators as Limerick won a first Munster SHC title since 1996. The celebrations contributed to a loss of focus, leading Clare to win the [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2013 All-Ireland SHC]] semi-final against Limerick at Croke Park. The [[2018 Limerick county hurling team season|2018 season]] concluded with Limerick winning the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2018 All-Ireland SHC]], the team's first since 1973, with a 3–16 to 2–18 point defeat of Galway in [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|the final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/new-green-wave-ends-45-years-of-heartache-for-limerick-863232.html |title =New green wave ends 45 years of heartache for Limerick|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=21 August 2018}} The team built on this success, winning the NHL in [[2019 National Hurling League|2019]], [[2020 National Hurling League|2020]] and [[2023 National Hurling League|2023]], the Munster SHC in [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|2019]], [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|2020]], [[2021 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|2021]] and [[2022 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2022]] and the All-Ireland SHC again in [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2020]], [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2021]] and [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2022]]. Munster Senior Hurling Championship 2023, All Ireland Hurling Championship 2023 to be forever remembered the team to join the Cork hurling Champions of the 40s and the Kilkenny hurling Champions of
